- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to historical mean.
- Underestimate late in the horizon; adjust final 5–10 days upward by 1–3% to account for mean reversion toward recent trends.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes (e.g., >85% of forecasted values after 80+), then correct by subtracting 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude from subsequent days.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- If forecast consistently lags true outcome by 2–3% over 10+ days, increase forecast by 0.5–1% per day to catch up with trend.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; if last 5 days are above 85%, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days to prevent momentum bias.
